title: callAsFunction & @dynamicCallable
jsBridge: `callAsFunction` makes a value callable like a function: `polynomial(2)`. JS gets this naturally (functions are objects with properties). Swift gives structs this ability while keeping their stored data typed.

compass.q: A JS function with extra properties (`fn.coefficients = …`) vs a Swift struct with `callAsFunction`: which is type-safe?
`callAsFunction` vs just storing a closure: when does a callable struct make sense?
`@dynamicCallable` vs `callAsFunction`: which is for dynamic-language interop?
SwiftUI's `DismissAction` is called like `dismiss()`. What mechanism makes that work?
